answer: The harbor holds work receipts rather than names, so the copper of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread. The anchor of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. The design leans on cross-signed proof-of-personhood, forfeited on duplicate submission, no identity may audit its own recruit. The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. Written in a short declarative sentences register, it stays short.
